title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 28 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 28 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 28 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 28.

questions.question: How old was Ahaz when he began to reign?
questions.explanation: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:1.

questions.question: Ahaz reigned for how many years in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: He reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, according to 2 Chronicles 28:1.

questions.question: True or False: Ahaz did what was right in the sight of the LORD.
questions.explanation: Ahaz did not that which was right in the sight of the LORD, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 28:1.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 28, who did Ahaz make molten images for?
questions.explanation: He made also molten images for Baalim, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:2.

questions.question: What did Ahaz do in the valley of the son of Hinnom?
options: Burnt his children in the fire
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt his children in the fire
questions.explanation: He burnt his children in the fire, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 28:3.

questions.question: True or False: Ahaz sacrificed and burnt incense in high places.
questions.explanation: He sacrificed also and burnt incense in the high places, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:4.

questions.question: Who delivered Ahaz into the hand of the king of Syria?
questions.explanation: The LORD his God delivered him into the hand of the king of Syria, according to 2 Chronicles 28:5.

questions.question: How many valiant men were slain in Judah by Pekah?
questions.explanation: Pekah slew in Judah an hundred and twenty thousand in one day, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:6.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Israel carried away 200,000 captives from Judah.
questions.explanation: The children of Israel carried away captive of their brethren two hundred thousand, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 28:8.

questions.question: What was the name of the prophet of the LORD mentioned in this chapter?
questions.explanation: A prophet of the LORD named Oded went out before the host that came to Samaria, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:9.

questions.question: What did the prophet Oded tell the children of Israel?
questions.explanation: Oded told them to deliver the captives again, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 28:11.

questions.question: True or False: Ahaz was a king who honored the traditions of his ancestors.
questions.explanation: Ahaz transgressed sore against the LORD, indicating he did not honor the traditions of his ancestors, as seen in 2 Chronicles 28:19.

questions.question: In what city did Ahaz sleep with his fathers?
questions.explanation: Ahaz slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of Jerusalem, according to 2 Chronicles 28:27.

questions.question: What did Ahaz do with the vessels of the house of God?
questions.explanation: Ahaz gathered together the vessels of the house of God and cut them in pieces, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:24.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 28, which event happens FIRST?
options: Ahaz is delivered into the hands of enemies
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned is that Ahaz reigned for 16 years in Jerusalem, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:1.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 28 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 28 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the age of Ahaz when he began to reign in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:1.

questions.question: What did Ahaz do that was not right in the sight of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Ahaz burnt his children in the fire, which is described as an abomination in 2 Chronicles 28:3.

questions.question: Which king of Israel smote Ahaz and Judah?
questions.explanation: Pekah the son of Remaliah slew a hundred and twenty thousand in Judah in one day, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:6.

questions.question: What did the prophet Oded warn the children of Israel about?
questions.explanation: Oded warned them that they should not keep the captives of Judah, as it would add to their sins against the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:10.

questions.question: What action did the heads of the children of Ephraim take against their captives?
questions.explanation: The heads of the children of Ephraim urged the captors to deliver the captives again to avoid adding to their sins, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:11.

questions.question: What did the armed men do with the captives and spoil?
questions.explanation: The armed men left the captives and the spoil before the princes and all the congregation, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:14.

questions.question: True or False: Ahaz asked the kings of Assyria for help.
questions.explanation: King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him during his distress, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 28:16.

questions.question: How did the Edomites affect Judah during Ahaz's reign?
questions.explanation: The Edomites smitten Judah and carried away captives, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:17.

questions.question: True or False: The Philistines invaded the cities of Judah during Ahaz's reign.
questions.explanation: The Philistines invaded the cities of the low country and the south of Judah, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:18.

questions.question: What was the response of Ahaz to the troubles he faced?
options: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus
questions.correctAnswer: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus
questions.explanation: Ahaz sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, believing they would help him, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:23.

questions.question: What did Ahaz do to the vessels of the house of God?
questions.explanation: Ahaz gathered together and cut in pieces the vessels of the house of God, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 28:24.

questions.question: What is stated about the rest of Ahaz's acts?
options: They are written in the book of the kings
questions.correctAnswer: They are written in the book of the kings
questions.explanation: The rest of Ahaz's acts and ways are recorded in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel, as noted in 2 Chronicles 28:26.

questions.question: True or False: Ahaz was buried in the sepulchres of the kings of Israel.
questions.explanation: Ahaz was not brought into the sepulchres of the kings of Israel, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:27.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 28 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 28.

questions.question: How old was Ahaz when he began to reign?
questions.explanation: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:1.

questions.question: What type of images did Ahaz make for Baalim?
questions.explanation: He made molten images for Baalim, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 28:2.

questions.question: What act did Ahaz commit in the valley of the son of Hinnom?
options: Burnt his children in the fire
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt his children in the fire
questions.explanation: Ahaz burnt his children in the fire after the abominations of the heathen, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:3.

questions.question: Who delivered Ahaz into the hand of the king of Syria?
questions.explanation: The LORD his God delivered him into the hand of the king of Syria, according to 2 Chronicles 28:5.

questions.question: Which king of Israel slew 120,000 valiant men in one day?
questions.explanation: Pekah the son of Remaliah slew in Judah a hundred and twenty thousand in one day, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:6.

questions.question: What did the prophet Oded tell the Israelites who came to Samaria?
options: To repent and return to Judah
questions.explanation: Oded told them to deliver the captives again, as he warned of the fierce wrath of the LORD upon them, seen in 2 Chronicles 28:11.

questions.question: Which king of Assyria did Ahaz seek help from?
questions.explanation: At that time did king Ahaz send unto the kings of Assyria for help, specifically Tiglathpileser, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:16.

questions.question: Which group invaded the cities of Judah during Ahaz's reign?
questions.explanation: The Philistines invaded the cities of the low country and the south of Judah, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 28:18.

questions.question: True or False: Ahaz strengthened himself in his distress.
questions.explanation: In the time of his distress, Ahaz did not strengthen himself but trespassed yet more against the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:22.

questions.question: What did Ahaz do to the vessels of the house of God?
options: Gave them to the king of Assyria
questions.explanation: Ahaz gathered together the vessels of the house of God and cut them in pieces, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 28:24.

questions.question: True or False: Ahaz was buried in the sepulchres of the kings of Israel.
questions.explanation: Ahaz was not brought into the sepulchres of the kings of Israel; he was buried in the city of Jerusalem, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:27.

questions.question: What significant act did Ahaz commit that was seen as provoking the LORD?
options: Made high places to burn incense
questions.correctAnswer: Made high places to burn incense
questions.explanation: Ahaz made high places to burn incense unto other gods, which provoked the LORD God of his fathers to anger, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:25.

questions.question: How did Ahaz's actions lead to the downfall of Judah, according to the chapter?
options: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus
questions.correctAnswer: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus
questions.explanation: Ahaz sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, believing they would help him, which ultimately led to his ruin and that of all Israel, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:23.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage relates to the theme of idol worship and its consequences seen in Ahaz's reign?
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:3-5 speaks of the commandment against having other gods before the LORD, which connects directly to Ahaz's idol worship and its consequences, as seen in 2 Chronicles 28.

questions.question: The term 'transgressed' as used to describe Ahaz's actions can be traced back to which Hebrew root word?
questions.explanation: 'Transgressed' is derived from the Hebrew word 'Pesha,' which means to violate or break a covenant, indicative of Ahaz's actions against the LORD, as reflected in 2 Chronicles 28:19.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 28 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 28 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was the age of Ahaz when he began to reign?
questions.explanation: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:1.

questions.question: Which false god did Ahaz make molten images for?
questions.explanation: Ahaz walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and made molten images for Baalim, according to 2 Chronicles 28:2.

questions.question: What abominable practice did Ahaz participate in?
options: Burning his children in the fire
questions.correctAnswer: Burning his children in the fire
questions.explanation: Ahaz burnt his children in the fire, which was an abomination according to 2 Chronicles 28:3.

questions.question: What was the result of Ahaz's actions regarding the worship of false gods?
options: Defeat by the king of Syria
questions.correctAnswer: Defeat by the king of Syria
questions.explanation: The LORD delivered Ahaz into the hand of the king of Syria as a consequence of his actions, as detailed in 2 Chronicles 28:5.

questions.question: How many valiant men were slain by Pekah in one day?
questions.explanation: Pekah the son of Remaliah slew an hundred and twenty thousand in one day, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:6.

questions.question: Who spoke to the army of Israel when they took captives?
questions.explanation: A prophet of the LORD named Oded spoke to the army of Israel, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:9.

questions.question: What did the heads of the children of Ephraim do upon hearing Oded's warning?
questions.explanation: The heads of the children of Ephraim stood up against the army and told them not to bring in the captives, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:12-14.

questions.question: What did Ahaz do with the vessels of the house of God?
questions.explanation: Ahaz gathered together and cut in pieces the vessels of the house of God, according to 2 Chronicles 28:24.

questions.question: How did Ahaz respond to the distress caused by the king of Assyria?
options: Gave tribute to the king of Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: Gave tribute to the king of Assyria
questions.explanation: Ahaz took away a portion out of the house of the LORD and gave it unto the king of Assyria, but it did not help him, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 28:21.

questions.question: What false gods did Ahaz sacrifice to?
questions.explanation: Ahaz sacrificed unto the gods of Damascus, believing they would help him, as stated in 2 Chronicles 28:23.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 28:19 reveal about the consequences of Ahaz's actions?
questions.explanation: The LORD brought Judah low because of Ahaz king of Israel, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:19.

questions.question: What can we learn about God's nature from Ahaz's reign?
questions.explanation: The chapter illustrates that the LORD punished Ahaz and Judah for their sins, as shown throughout the chapter, especially in verses 5 and 19.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated through the judgment on Judah?
questions.explanation: The judgment on Judah for their sins shows God's holiness and intolerance for sin, as indicated in verses like 28:3 and 28:19.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be drawn from the actions of Ahaz and the response of the Ephraimites?
questions.explanation: Ahaz's sin led to the captivity of Judah, while the response of the Ephraimites highlights that they too recognized the consequences of further sin, as seen in verses 10-13.

questions.question: What overarching theme does the chapter convey about the leadership of Ahaz?
questions.explanation: The chapter consistently emphasizes Ahaz's idolatry and the resulting consequences for Judah, as depicted in multiple verses including 28:2-4.
